fix(store): grant group bits to unreadable directories on macOS
prs.author: JhonHawk
prs.body:
## Summary

On macOS, `pnpm install` fails with `EISDIR` when it creates a store directory that its owner cannot read, which happens in a group-writable store under a umask that removes owner read (such as `0o477`). The path was added in https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/15882.

- Cause: Node's `fs.lchmodSync` on macOS opens the path with `O_WRONLY | O_SYMLINK` before `fchmod`. `open(2)` with `O_WRONLY` fails with `EISDIR` for every directory, whatever its mode, so the macOS branch of `addUnreadableDirModeBits` could never succeed.
- Fix: the macOS branch now opens the directory with `O_SEARCH` (`O_EXEC | O_DIRECTORY`), which needs no read access, plus `O_NOFOLLOW`, then `fstat`s and `fchmod`s that descriptor. A directory swapped for a symlink is still refused. The macOS and Linux branches share one helper and differ only in how they open the handle and change its mode.
- The helper now compares the owner with the effective uid, which owns the directories pnpm creates, as pnpm v12 does (`pnpm/crates/fs/src/file_mode/directory.rs`).
- pnpm v12 is not affected: it already opens these directories with `O_SEARCH` and uses `fchmodat`.

Verification on macOS 27 with Node 24.19.0:
- The existing test `directories added to a group-writable store get group access under a umask that removes owner read` in `@pnpm/store.cafs` failed with `EISDIR` before the fix and passes after it. All 145 `@pnpm/store.cafs` tests pass.
- `@pnpm/store.file-mode` compiles and lints clean.

prs.title: fix(importer): take one swap lock per install instead of one per target
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Related to pnpm/tasks#156 (items 2 and 3).

The swap lock that pnpm/pnpm#17091 added to the package importer was keyed by the target directory: every forced replacement of an occupied package paid a lock acquisition and left a permanent held file under the per-user lock root, one per package per project path. This PR replaces it with one lock per install.

- `ModulesSwapLock` is keyed by the install's modules directory, taken on the first forced import of a private target (including into an absent one, so every hoisted install and every `--force` install takes it once) and released when the linking phase ends, before any lifecycle script runs, so an install a script starts in the same project does not wait on its parent. One acquisition and one held file per install; none for an isolated install that forces nothing. An install that cannot take the lock, or whose wait runs out, replaces unserialized for the rest of its life rather than waiting again on every import.
- Each install path owns the lock for its linking phase and hands a reference down through `InstallCaches` and `PackageImportOptions`, next to `logged_methods`. The build phase's rare side-effects re-materialization takes a lock of its own only around that one import.
- The absent-target fast path holds it too, so two forced installs of one project take turns for their whole replacement phase. That closes the move-aside fallback's vacancy for forced importers, which pnpm/pnpm#17091 left open on Windows.
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(deploy): stop writing a second copy of every package on macOS
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17116.

On macOS, `pnpm deploy` left a `node_modules/.pnpm/@/` tree in the deploy directory with a second copy of every registry package. Nothing linked to it, so deploy output doubled in size for nothing.

The macOS directory-clone cache puts each package in a canonical slot under `global_virtual_store_dir`, then clones it into the virtual store. A deploy points `global_virtual_store_dir` at its own `node_modules/.pnpm`, so the canonical slots ended up inside the deploy. `DirCloneCache::eligible` now turns the cache down when the canonical root is the virtual store itself. The deploy falls back to the per-file import, the same thing it does with `packageImportMethod: hardlink`. pnpm v11 has no such cache, so this is v12 only.

Tests:
- `dir_clone_cache::tests::not_eligible_when_the_canonical_root_is_the_virtual_store` (unit).
- `deploy::deploy_from_shared_lockfile_installs_selected_project` now also checks that `.pnpm` has no GVS-shaped `@`/`@scope` directories.
- Both fail on macOS without the fix. I also ran the issue's repro script with the built binary: 3 package copies, no `.pnpm/@`, no dangling links.

Since `pnpm/pnpm#17067`, `packages:` records every declared `peerDependency` even when a package resolves that peer from its own `dependencies` rather than binding an external provider in its peer suffix.

This PR finishes the remaining lockfile peer-binding consumers tracked in `pnpm/tasks#143` across both v12 (Rust) and v11 (TypeScript):

prs.title: fix(deps-resolver): memoise hashed peer bindings and scope cross-importer reuse decline
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17137 addressing review feedback:

- Track descendant visits in `collect_descendant_targets` by `HashMap<PkgNameVerPeer, HashSet<usize>>` so reaching a shared descendant through one branch does not prevent another branch carrying a different transitive peer from recording its peer target, while `MAX_VISITED_SNAPSHOTS` counts distinct snapshots.
- Memoise `BoundProviders::of_snapshot` per hashed `PkgNameVerPeer` across workspace resolution (`WorkspaceCacheState`), locked-peer recovery (`LockedPeersIndex::from_lockfile`), and `pnpm deploy` (`bind_singleton_peers`).
- Scope `changed_direct_deps` per importer and check `changed_direct_dep_versions` in `reused_parent_has_changed_direct_child` (resolving aliased `SnapshotDepRef` targets) while keeping `preseed_one_changed_direct` scoped to the importer's own `changed_direct_deps` during concurrent preseeding, and declining reuse only at the affected parent node rather than every ancestor in `SubtreeWalk`.

**Version scope:** pnpm v12 (Rust / pacquet) only. pnpm v11 (TypeScript) is unaffected because `@pnpm/installing.deps-resolver` resolves all workspace importers in a single `resolveDependencies` pass and does not use `BoundProviders::of_snapshot` or `WorkspaceTreeCtx` subtree-reuse gates.

prs.title: fix(lockfile): accept an aliased file: child of an injected package
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17130.

With `injectWorkspacePackages: true` and `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, an injected package that depends on a local directory under another name (`"renamed": "file:../b"`) gets the child recorded as `renamed: b@file:../b`. The freshness check from pnpm/pnpm#17065 passed that ref to `getLocalPath`, which only accepted refs starting with `file:` or `link:`, so the path never matched and a frozen install right after a normal one failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. `getLocalPath` now also reads the path from a `name@file:` ref, the way pnpm v12 already reads it from an aliased lockfile ref.

I reproduced it with the v11 CLI built from main: `pnpm install` in the issue's layout, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in `app` fails with "The dependencies of local directory dependency "a" do not match the lockfile". With the fix it passes, and pointing the child at another directory still fails. The new test in `allProjectsAreUpToDate.test.ts` fails without the fix. pnpm/pnpm#17065 shipped in v11.28.6, so the PR includes a changeset.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
An injected package's file: child installed under another alias is

with file: or link:, so the freshness check could not compare the path
```

prs.title: fix(lockfile): check transitive local directory dependencies on a frozen install
prs.author: charan-rathore
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes pnpm/pnpm#17128.

#17065 made a frozen install compare an injected workspace package's immediate dependencies with its lockfile snapshot. A directory dependency one level deeper is still only checked by path: `childIsUpToDate` resolves a `link:`/`file:`/`workspace:` child against the recorded spec and stops there. So when `b/package.json` moves from `leaf: file:../leaf1` to `leaf: file:../leaf2`, the frozen install validates, leaves the consumer lockfile untouched, and installs the stale `leaf@1.0.0`.

This change recurses: after a local child spec still matches, the child's own lockfile snapshot is validated with the same freshness check, with the peer-alias scope accumulated from every ancestor, as the resolver does. A snapshot is checked once per peer scope, which cuts cycles without skipping a shared directory reached where different peers are in scope. Links keep their current treatment (they carry no dependency snapshot to validate), and the children compared are still the resolver's non-dev wanted dependencies, so excluded dependency groups are unaffected.

Regression tests cover an unchanged chain (valid), a transitive directory whose own dependencies changed (reported; the test fails without the source change), and a directory dependency cycle (terminates). ## Summary

On v12 a token passed as `--config.//<host>/:_authToken=<token>` is ignored. `pnpm add` against a private registry fails with `HTTP status client error (401 Unauthorized)`, and `pnpm publish` to a registry that doesn't require auth goes out anonymously.

[`ConfigOverrides::set`](pnpm/crates/cli/src/config_overrides.rs#L289-L309) only handles `@scope:registry` out of the `--config.` keys. The other npmrc keys end up in `unported`, which only the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` schema reads, so auth and TLS keys like `//host/:_authToken` or `strict-ssl` are dropped. The raw tokens reach `Config::raw_cli_config` too, but only after the auth sources were merged.

prs.title: fix(config): centralize reconciliation of config dependencies
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm install` now reconciles removed config dependencies, including removal of the entire setting. It removes stale links and unused env-lockfile entries; frozen installs reject stale roots before mutation. Other commands bootstrap config dependencies without dropping locked roots, so diagnostics such as `audit signatures` can still inspect them.

The refactor gives both implementations an explicit bootstrap/reconcile mode and a shared state loader. The loader decides whether work is needed before store/resolver setup, and the loaded env lockfile is passed into resolution. Installation and exclusion pruning share declared-root retention and the existing graph pruner. Reconciliation traverses the graph only when state changes. The Rust repeat-install fast path uses the same state loader.

Package-manager roots retain their graph, including when they pin a different version of a package also used as a config dependency. The existing verifier and installer still handle integrity, policy checks, writing, and materialization. The lockfile format is unchanged, and the Rust graph helper stays in the lockfile crate to avoid a package-manager/env-installer dependency cycle.

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17144. Covers both pnpm v11 and v12.

prs.title: fix(patching): apply and commit patches that rename a file
prs.author: maxymlyskov
prs.body:
## Summary

Renaming or moving a file in a `pnpm patch` edit dir breaks `pnpm patch-commit`, and every install after it.

`patch-commit` rewrites the temp folders in its diff to package paths, but `is_diff_path_line` only matches `diff --git`, `---` and `+++`, so the `rename from` / `rename to` lines keep the absolute temp paths. And `apply_one_file` refuses every `FileOperation::Rename` anyway. The patch is already in `patchedDependencies` by then, so every later install fails the same way. A rename patch written by pnpm 11 fails on pnpm 12 too.

```sh
# package.json: { "dependencies": { "is-positive": "3.1.0" } }
pnpm patch is-positive@3.1.0 --edit-dir edit
mv edit/index.js edit/main.js   # and set "main" to main.js
pnpm patch-commit edit
# main: exit 1, "rename/copy operations in patches are not yet supported",
#   and the patch has `rename from <store>/tmp/patch-commit/<hash>/index.js`
# this branch: exit 0, `rename from index.js` / `rename to main.js`,
#   the same patch file pnpm 11.28.6 writes
rm -rf node_modules && pnpm install
# main: exit 1, every time. this branch: exit 0, node_modules/is-positive has main.js
```

The fix: `rename from ` and `rename to ` count as path lines in `patch-commit`, and the applier handles `Rename`. diffy gives rename paths without the `a/` / `b/` prefix, so `package_relative_operation` doesn't strip them (stripping would turn `lib/a.js` into `a.js`). Both paths still go through `resolve_target`.

prs.title: fix(pack): expand numeric brace ranges
prs.author: shuaiyafei
prs.body:
## Summary

Package file patterns such as `part{1..3}.js` currently miss the numbered files
in pnpm v12. The shared ignore-rule parser treats a brace group without a comma
as literal text. The same gap makes numeric range exclusions in `.npmignore`
and `.gitignore` ineffective. npm and pnpm v11 already expand these ranges.

Extend the existing brace expander with numeric and single-letter sequences,
including descending bounds, steps, and zero padding. This builds on the shared package
selection compiler from pnpm/pnpm#17135 and retains its alternative and byte
limits.

Review follow-up in `26975db`: a zero step defaults to 1. Padding in a step
enables zero padding to the endpoint width. Both behaviors were checked against
the repository's locked `brace-expansion` dependency.

Review follow-up in `abfe121`: single-letter sequences such as `{a..c}` expand
as in `brace-expansion`. Numeric padding no longer goes through the `{:0width$}`
formatter, which panicked above a width of 65535 that the byte limit admits.

Nested literal brace groups are rejected as range candidates before their
contents are split, avoiding repeated scans of inner groups.

For a package containing `part1.js`, `part2.js`, `part3.js`, and `part4.js`:

```json
{ "files": ["part{1..3}.js"] }
```

The first three files now ship. `part4.js` stays out.

Fixes three `pnpm prune` bug areas across pnpm v11 (TypeScript) and pnpm v12 (Rust):

## Summary

Fixes pnpm/tasks#170.

The v11 `pnpm sbom` command now reads the dedicated lockfiles of selected workspace projects and their reachable workspace dependencies. It rekeys importers relative to the workspace root, merges package entries, and rejects missing or conflicting entries. Directory package metadata is read relative to its owning project. This covers unfiltered, filtered, recursive, and split SBOM output.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Load dedicated lockfiles for selected and reachable workspace projects when
sharedWorkspaceLockfile is false. Re-key their importers to the workspace root
before SBOM collection, and merge package entries without losing required
package status. Reject conflicting package data to avoid emitting an inaccurate
SBOM. Fail when a selected or reachable project lacks a lockfile importer.
Read directory package metadata relative to the project that owns its lockfile.

Fixes pnpm/tasks#170.
```
